subject: Sandbox endpoints & rateguard: next steps and action items
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Smith <laura@payflux.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom@payflux.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sandbox endpoints & rateguard: next steps and action items

Hi Laura / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — appreciate the thoughtful questions. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have clear owners: 

What we covered (high level):
- Hosted API as the quick evaluation path (no infra changes).
- Endpoints you’ll likely need: chat/completions for customer responses, embeddings for semantic search, and a lightweight reranking endpoint.
- Default rateguard behavior: per-endpoint token and request ceilings, short burst smoothing, and automatic fallback to lower-cost model variants when needed.

Action items I suggest for a 2-week sandbox:
1) Confirm traffic profile (expected steady qps and expected peak bursts).
2) Map endpoints to dev teams (chat vs embeddings vs rerank).
3) Provide a short sample workload (3–5 representative requests) so we can pre-warm KV/prefix cache.
4) Kick off sandbox access — I’ve attached a one-page checklist to speed provisioning.

Two quick operational notes: we can support short bursts above the default limits during a hosted trial (we do this for pilots) — we’ll coordinate with infra. Dedicated is typically recommended if you’re planning sustained throughput > ~100 r/s or need strict tenant isolation. For most evaluations the Hosted path is faster and lower friction.

Can you confirm:
- Expected sustained qps (avg) and peak qps (burst)?
- Any strict data residency or encryption constraints for this initial pilot?

I’ll loop Karthik to propose a short technical sync to map endpoints and sample payloads. Monica will own onboarding and access tickets.

Attachments: redwood_sandbox_quickstart_v1.pdf (1 page checklist)
HubSpot deal: PF-2025-058

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
From: Laura Smith <laura@payflux.com>

Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom@payflux.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sandbox endpoints & rateguard: next steps and action items

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers inline: 

- Traffic profile: our initial pilot (customer search + chat assistant) is expected to be ~15 requests/sec sustained during business hours with short bursts up to ~60 req/s when marketing sends traffic spikes. Payloads are moderate (mostly short prompts + metadata).
- Latency: target 200–300ms p50 for chat responses; p95 can be higher but ideally under 1s.
- Data residency: for the pilot we’re fine with US-hosted evaluation; long-term we’ll need EU + US tenancy options for regional customers.

A couple of questions: 
1) What are the default hosted rate limits we’ll hit for a sandbox account?
2) How do you handle burst smoothing — is there a queue or token-bucket approach?
3) If we need to move to Dedicated later, how disruptive is the migration for endpoints & client integration?

We’re happy to do the 2-week sandbox. Can Karthik join a 30-min technical sync this week? Tom and I are available Wed/Thu morning PST.

Thanks —
Laura Smith
Director of Product, PayFlux
laura@payflux.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Smith <laura@payflux.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom@payflux.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sandbox endpoints & rateguard: next steps and action items

Laura —

Great — those numbers are super helpful and well within a hosted pilot. Short answers: 

1) Default sandbox rate limits: typically 20 r/s per sandbox endpoint, with token-based ceilings for long completions. We can temporarily lift the per-endpoint qps for your pilot to match the 15r/s sustained + 60r/s burst you described.
2) Burst smoothing: we use a hybrid token-bucket + short-term queue (few hundred ms) approach so short spikes are absorbed without rejecting well-behaved clients. For very large sustained bursts we will throttle to preserve latency SLOs for other tenants unless you move to Dedicated.
3) Migration to Dedicated: client-side integration is largely unchanged (same API surface). Migration steps: model pinning, routing policy update, and DNS/endpoint swap. We typically plan a blue-green switchover — minimal app changes.

Next operational items: 
- I’ll kick off sandbox provisioning once you confirm the pilot window (propose Wed 16 Jul — Thu 31 Jul).
- Please fill this short usage capture doc so Karthik can pre-configure caches and batching: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1example-usage-capture
- Karthik — can you propose two 30-min slots Wed/Thu 10:00–11:30 PST?

Monica will send the access ticket and attach the standard pilot terms (short, non-binding).

Ben

Ben / Monica —

Thanks — I’ll take lead on the tech sync. Proposed plan:
- Tech sync (30 min): confirm endpoint mapping (chat/embeddings/rerank), sample payloads, target token sizes.
- Pre-config: I’ll set up endpoint profiles with increased qps for the pilot window and pre-warm prefix/KV caches against the sample requests.
- Rateguard plan: baseline 20 r/s per endpoint, raise to requested sustained 15 r/s with 60 r/s burst allowance for the first 2 weeks. I’ll document expected p50/p95 and fallback behavior.
- Migration note for sales: recommend Dedicated if they expect sustained > 100 r/s or require tenant-isolated encryption keys / on-prem.

I’m available Wed 16 Jul 10:30 or Thu 17 Jul 09:30 PST — I’ll send a calendar invite for Wed 10:30 unless you tell me otherwise.
